strategy_name: Stocks-in-Play universe filter (high relative volume + catalyst episodes)
setup_summary: Universe/regime gate before any strategy applies: pre-market gap >=2% or intraday move >=$1, average relative volume >=1.5x normal, ATR >= $0.50 (min volatility), average daily volume >=500k (min liquidity), short interest <30% (avoid squeeze exposure), and a fundamental catalyst (news/earnings/FDA/M&A). Trade only instruments in this state; a stock trading at normal volume is dominated by HFT and not tradeable.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = high-relative-volume episode with catalyst. Invalidation = relative volume returns to normal / no catalyst / moves are choppy without directional foreshadowing — stay out.
risk_geometry: N/A (universe selection filter, not an entry geometry); feeds instrument and episode selection before strategy-specific stops/targets apply.
quote: Retail traders trade only Stocks in Play, high relative volume stocks that have fundamental catalysts and are being traded regardless of the overall market.
chapter_anchor: Ch 4 (How to Find Stocks for Trades; Rule 7), lines 497-706
notes: For a single-instrument BTCUSDT tape this is an episodic regime filter rather than a cross-sectional stock screen: the participation feature group should capture relative-volume spikes, ATR expansion, and catalyst windows (news, ETF flows, funding spikes). The book's anti-correlation principle ('independent of sector and overall market') maps to a cross-market feature (BTC vs alt/market beta) — candidates for the participation and cross_market feature groups.
book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

strategy_name: Risk Reversal Extremes as Contrarian Sentiment
mechanism: 25-delta risk reversals embed market positioning; at extreme values (one standard deviation from the average) they signal overcrowding and give contrarian reversal signals.
setup_summary: Track the 25-delta call/put risk reversal (IV skew) for the instrument; readings at or beyond 1 std dev from the rolling average mark overbought/oversold positioning and favor fading the direction of the skew; near-zero readings indicate no bias (range conditions).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: RR extreme reached. Invalidation: RR continues to extend, implying positioning is still building rather than reversing (trend confirmation).
risk_geometry: No price geometry in the book; contrarian directional filter only.
quote: We identify extreme levels as one standard deviation plus or minus the average risk reversal. When risk reversals are at these levels, they give off contrarian signals.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, 'Fundamental Trading Strategy: Risk Reversals', p. 112-114 (also Ch. 7, p. 68-69)
notes: Crypto analog is Deribit 25-delta options skew for BTC; V8's current tape has no options data, so this is data-blocked until an options/skew feed lands. Would be a participation-group positioning feature.
book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

strategy_name: lunar-phase buy-sell cycle (new moon buy, full moon sell)
mechanism: the first half of the lunar month is an accumulation phase and the second half a distribution phase; index returns are systematically higher from new moon to full moon than the reverse
setup_summary: Buy at the new moon (Sun-Moon 0-degree conjunction) and sell at the next full moon (180-degree opposition, ~14-16 days). Cited RBS study: FTSE new->full moon trading turned GBP 1,000 (1984) into GBP 12,116 vs GBP 5,130 buy-hold; DAX/HSI 'even more profitable'; S&P higher since 1928. Mikula backtest: new-moon entry + full-moon exit combined with stochastic on soybean futures, 44 trades, 66% profitable (longs 54%, shorts 88%). Book advises using it only as a filter: buy when the new moon coincides with a technical buy (e.g. stochastic < 20), sell when the full moon coincides with a technical sell (stochastic > 80), and stand aside otherwise. Falsifiable: the new->full moon half-period of the synodic month has positive average return vs the full->new half.
trigger_invalidation: Lunar timing 'can become a trap if the market enters a bear phase'; if no accumulation occurs in the first half of the lunar month, treat as a larger-trend change warning.
risk_geometry: Fixed ~14-16 day swing hold; protective stops via technical analysis; book says 'the intention is not to trade on the basis of moon-phased buy-sell signals only'.
quote: buying FTSE on the new moon and selling on the full moon, this would result in GBP12,116 overall figure for the same period
chapter_anchor: Ch 9 'Using Lunar Cycles in Trading'; Ch 2 'Financial Astrology'
notes: Secondhand bank-report correlation, no controlled test; V8 forbids wall-clock in replay and the claim is equity-index based, so it is gated on a calendar/cycle feature group with low prior. Lunar phase is computable from bar date metadata if ever admitted.
book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

strategy_name: Accumulation/distribution: high-volume stagnant-price sessions at extremes
mechanism: high volume with stagnant price at an extreme reveals absorption: one side's ammunition is spent
setup_summary: At a low price level after a decline, a session with heavy volume and a tiny real body (spinning top) that pushes a new low but cannot sustain it = accumulation (bears sell into full force yet price stagnates; all supply absorbed) - long bias, confirmed by a following rally. Mirror at highs = distribution - topping bias. The small body is required to establish 'stagnant prices'.
trigger_invalidation: Accumulation fails if price closes below the absorbing session's low; distribution fails if price closes above the absorbing session's high.
risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation after the absorbing session; stop below the accumulation low (or above the distribution high).
quote: Accumulation occurs when, at a low price level, there is a high volume session with stagnant prices... All that the bears have tried to sell has been accumulated by the bulls.
chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Accumulation and Distribution', pp.42-44
notes: The price geometry (high volume + tiny body at an extreme) is deterministic, but exchange-reported perp volume is a weak signal (wash trading, aggregate prints), so this stays backlog until the participation feature is trusted. Conceptually overlaps Wyckoff accumulation/distribution, likely corroborated by other books in this library.
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: The playing field: spread drag and target-sizing game theory
mechanism: the spread is the house edge (roulette zero pockets); with a fixed spread, small targets suffer massively worse raw odds than large targets, because the spread is a larger fraction of the move - target size is a first-order determinant of win probability before any strategy
setup_summary: Quantitative lesson, not a trade: with a 3-pip spread, a trader targeting +10 pips needs a 13-pip favorable move but loses 10 pips on only a 7-pip adverse move (raw odds 1.857:1 against); targeting +100 pips needs 103 vs 97 (raw odds 1.06:1). Larger targets and longer holds shrink the spread's relative drag; traders are also paid the spread less often. A 6%/month goal compounds to ~100%/year; use a monthly 'account stop' (stop trading for the month when gains retrace to the goal level).
trigger_invalidation: N/A - methodology lesson; applies to how experts are sized and how the simulator cost model treats fees.
risk_geometry: N/A. Sizing/odds lesson: never accept spreads >5 pips for small-target trades; prefer R-multiples large enough that fees/funding/spread are a small fraction of the target.
quote: in order to turn a profit of 10 pips, the trader actually needs the exchange rate to move 13 pips in his or her favor: 10 + 3 = 13... an adverse move of just 7 pips will result in an equivalent loss of 10 pips... The 'raw odds' of 10-pip win versus a 10-pip loss... 13/7 = 1.857 : 1
chapter_anchor: Chapter 18 'The Forex Playing Field', pp.215-222
notes: Directly relevant to V8's economic verdict discipline: the simulator's Binance USDM cost model (taker/maker fees ~2-10bps + funding) is the crypto analogue of the spread, and it must be an explicit term in expert evaluation. Supports V8's target_r>=1.0 R-multiple convention and argues against low-target variants. Also a caution for the funding_carry expert: leverage magnifies the carry yield on capital (collecting 3.5% on the full notional while posting a fraction) - the same math that makes funding collection on perps attractive.
book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

strategy_name: Scheduled-Event Straddle (earnings straddle)
mechanism: Scheduled binary events expand volatility; buying both call and put before the event profits from any large move because the in-the-money leg gains more (rising delta) than the out-of-the-money leg loses (falling delta).
setup_summary: For a stock with earnings 3 trading days away that reports after the bell, trades >1M shares/day, beta >=2.0, price >=$40, and gapped >$1.00 at its last two earnings: if 2-of-3 oscillators (RSI(5)<30/>70, Stoch %K(5)<25/>75, CCI(20)<-100/>+100) show oversold/overbought, buy the anticipated-side option 3 days pre-earnings and the opposite side at earnings-day close (same, nearest strike); otherwise buy both sides before the earnings close. Profit requires a gap >$0.50-$1.00 at the event open.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: event 3 sessions out + 2-of-3 oscillator extreme (or no extreme -> buy both sides). Invalidation: event gap <$0.50 at open (judgment call, smaller returns); quiet market cycle where volatile stocks do not move on earnings; position capped at 5 trading days post-event.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy-at-close, nearest same strike, both sides (option premium at risk only, no stop). Target: post-event gap run; exit losing side at open, hold winner, exit at close of 5th trading day after announcement. Expiry: 5 bars hard cap + option expiration rules.
quote: as long as the stock moves big, we should always show a proﬁt on the trade because of the delta factor, and normally that proﬁt is large enough to cover commissions and the spread and still post a solid double-digit-percentage winner
chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - The Straddle (pp. 283-308; file lines 1-294)
notes: Requires options (delta asymmetry) and a scheduled-event calendar; perp crypto has neither earnings nor listed options on most venues. Template could map to macro events (FOMC/CPI) with Deribit options, but is outside the perp-futures scope. Book states this works only in a 12-16 week earnings-season window.
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Delta / Cumulative Delta Volume (Bid-Ask Order Flow)
mechanism: order_flow_dominance
setup_summary: Per bar, delta = (volume traded at the ask) - (volume traded at the bid); cumulative delta sums per-bar deltas over a window and is displayed as a series to show net buying/selling pressure. Divergence between price and cumulative delta (price makes a new high while cumulative delta fails to) flags weakening buying. Proposed as a feature input for the flow feature group rather than a standalone strategy.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (feature input, not an entry rule).
risk_geometry: Feature input only; no entry/stop/target geometry.
quote: delta volume refers to the difference in volumes between those contracts that trade at the 'ask' and those that trade at the 'bid'... the net difference between the two then displayed as 'delta'.
chapter_anchor: Ch 12, 'Delta Volume' and 'Cumulative Delta Volume'
notes: The author states she has not used delta/cumulative delta and 'cannot comment on their validity', hence NARRATIVE evidence. Crypto perp venues publish taker buy/sell volume, so the raw data exists, but V8's 1h OHLCV tape would need an additional field (e.g., taker_base_volume) to build this feature. No expert proposed until the feature exists and is screened.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Volume Baseline Calibration (High/Low/Average per Instrument)
mechanism: volume_normalization
setup_summary: Before judging any volume bar as high, low, or average, calibrate the volume distribution for the instrument and session; an extreme volume bar early in a window (e.g., a news spike) distorts the relative reading of all subsequent bars in that session. Compare each bar against a windowed baseline that is robust to such distortion events.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (methodology rule).
risk_geometry: N/A - informs feature construction, not trade geometry.
quote: we must try to have an idea of what is considered to be high, low and average volume. So that when these extremes of volume do appear, they do not distort our view of what follows in the remainder of the trading session.
chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.21 (Coffee 80-tick) - the 'always remember' caveat
notes: Directly informs how V8 should compute volume features: prefer percentile or robust-window baselines over naive windowed means so extreme bars (liquidation cascades, listing events) do not poison subsequent readings. Relevant to the volume/participation feature groups and any simulator volume model.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Equivolume / Candle-Volume Charts - Time as a Cause Dimension
mechanism: time_as_cause_dimension
setup_summary: Equivolume charts replace the time axis with volume (box width = volume, box height = high-low); candle-volume charts overlay equivolume boxes on OHLC candles. The author's own critique: removing time removes Wyckoff's cause-and-effect, the core of trend-power assessment - 'time is the third element of the volume and price relationship' - so the approach becomes two-dimensional.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (presentation technique, no entry logic).
risk_geometry: N/A.
quote: as Wykcoff himself stated, it is the cause and effect which holds the key to the development of the trend. In other words, time is the third element of the volume and price relationship. Remove time, and the approach becomes two dimensional.
chapter_anchor: Ch 12, 'Equivolume Charts' and 'Candle Volume Charts'
notes: Presentation-layer techniques with no signal logic to port to V8. The lesson is architectural and aligns with V8's determinism rules: keep time (event/available/ingested clocks) as a first-class dimension and never collapse it; a volume-scaled-bar display encodes nothing beyond what OHLCV + volume already carry. DEFER_GATED unless a display feature is ever requested.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Volume-at-price (VAP) density as support/resistance significance
mechanism: the vertical distribution of traded volume at each price level quantifies where supply/demand is dense; high-density price regions act as significant support/resistance, and the depth of the volume platform determines how hard a level is to break and where stops belong.
setup_summary: Compute a VAP histogram over a window; price levels with extreme volume density (especially old, long-lived congestion) act as barriers. A breakout through a high-density platform requires extreme volume; a low-density region takes little effort to penetrate. Price stalled in congestion on ultra-high volume that fails to advance implies selling pressure/weakness. Long-lived congestion with extreme density = strong support platform (stop placement and target guidance).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price approaching or stalling in a high-VAP-density zone. Invalidation: density read without the time component (duration matters - 3 days of congestion is a heavier platform than a few hours at the same visual density); levels treated as rigid rather than elastic.
risk_geometry: VAP depth directly informs stop placement (the book uses the density of the support platform to gauge where stops go) and target selection (next volume-dense platform); no entry-level stop/target stated.
quote: If the concentration of volume was at the bottom, then this is more likely to be buying volume rather than selling volume.
chapter_anchor: Ch.9 - Volume At Price (VAP)
notes: Crypto perps report real traded volume (unlike the FX tick-volume proxy the book needs), so VAP density is directly computable from the perp tape. Propose VAP-derived features (high-volume nodes, density-weighted S/R levels) for the location feature group; could later seed a volume_profile expert.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: 1% risk rule + stop below signal wick/congestion floor
mechanism: financial risk is quantifiable and capped (1% rule); stop placement follows market-set natural levels (the signal candle's wick or the floor of the volume-backed support zone), so risk is defined by structure rather than by arbitrary distance.
setup_summary: Risk rules stated across the book: cap per-trade financial risk with simple money management such as the 1% rule; place the stop below the wick of the reversal signal candle (e.g., the hammer low) or in the lower regions of the congestion/support zone; use the VAP density/depth of the support platform to judge where the stop should sit; a validated breakout gives a 'natural floor' that protects the position and is where stops belong.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - risk rule, not a signal. Applies to every position: stop below structure, size so the stop distance risks ~1% of capital.
risk_geometry: Stop: below signal-candle wick or below the congestion floor; size: such that the stop-distance loss is ~1% of capital; targets: next volume-dense platform / natural S/R.
quote: Any stop loss by the way would be below the wick of the hammer, with the market setting this level for us.
chapter_anchor: Ch.4 - risk on the trade; Ch.7 - stop placement; Ch.10 - SLV worked example
notes: Direct input to RiskGate: per-exposure sizing tied to structure-defined stop distance and a per-trade risk cap; the 1% figure is a practitioner heuristic, not an empirical optimum.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Crisis hunting: positive-skew harvesting of rare events
mechanism: Rare events are systematically underpriced (the rarer, the more undervalued), so engineer a payoff profile that loses small and frequent and pays large and rare
setup_summary: Construct every expert's risk_geometry with positive skew: bounded small frequent losses (tight stop, small R) against rare large gains (wide target, large R), so expectation is positive even at a win rate below 50%. On BTCUSDT 1h this is the payoff profile of tight-stop trend/crisis-hunting variants that let tails pay. The book also states the binding companion rule (Nero): never expose to a loss exceeding a fixed cap 'regardless of the probability of such an event' — i.e., no unbounded-loss (short-convexity) position is ever admissible.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any setup whose payoff is constructed asymmetric-positive. Invalid: expectation goes negative under honest fat-tail calibration (Monte Carlo with realistic kurtosis), or realized drawdown breaches the designed bounded cap.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close or limit at tail levels; stop: small R (tight ATR multiple); target: large R-multiple, left open so rare moves pay; expiry: long/open-ended. Book states only the payoff profile (small frequent losses, rare large gains); R-multiples are V8's expression.
quote: I try to make money infrequently, as infrequently as possible, simply because I believe that rare events are not fairly valued, and that the rarer the event, the more undervalued it will be in price.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Rare Events (p. 89); Nero's cap in Ch. 1 (p. 15)
notes: Book-side quantitative case: 999/1000 chance of +$1 vs 1/1000 chance of -$10,000 is a -$9 expectation. 'Premium sellers eat like chickens and go to the bathroom like elephants' — most option sellers blow up. For perps (no native options), the positive-skew posture is expressed via asymmetric R-multiples and hard max-loss caps; high leverage makes the bounded-loss rule mandatory.
book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

strategy_name: Four-outcome payout: small losses dominate, rare large profits carry returns
setup_summary: There are only four trade outcomes: big losses (prevented by immediate stops), small losses (the majority, typically -0.2% to -1.2%), small profits (0.2-1.2%), and rare large profits (2-14.5% over multi-month holds) which pay for all the small losses. Low win rate is expected and irrelevant. Falsifiable: over a long sample, the PnL distribution is highly right-skewed with a majority of small negative trades and a small tail of large winners.
trigger_invalidation: None; an expectancy property.
risk_geometry: No geometry; defines the expected payoff shape that screening thresholds and expectancy accounting should assume for a trend-following Expert.
quote: There are only 4 possibilities when trading. One can have big losses, small losses, small profits, and rare large profits.
chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, p.164 (journal-wide confirmation p.192)
notes: Should inform V8's simulator/screening assumptions: an Expert of the breakout family should not be judged on win rate but on the fat right tail; position-scaling that adds contracts when a trade is working amplifies the tail (documented in silver/gold entries). Also justifies tolerance for long drawdown phases (17 months) before any verdict.
book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

strategy_name: Stop-loss semantics differ in 24/7 markets (closed-market gap risk vanishes)
mechanism: equities stop-losses give no protection when the market is closed and gaps can run through stops; 24/7 perp trading removes closed-market gap risk, changing the stop-loss risk profile
setup_summary: Methodology lesson: the book repeatedly warns that stop-loss orders 'do not provide any guarantees for how and when they will be executed, and they provide no coverage when the market is closed' and that news can gap price through a stop level. In 24/7 crypto perps the closed-market gap window is structurally absent, so stop-losses on bar-close/limit fills behave differently from the book's equities model; the residual tail risks are liquidation cascades, funding shocks, and exchange outages rather than overnight gaps.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - methodology affecting risk-rule and simulator calibration (the V8 simulator's gap semantics should model 24/7 continuous trading, not equity-style overnight gaps).
risk_geometry: Stops execute continuously; sizing must still account for liquidation cascades and leverage-triggered waterfall moves that take the place of gap risk.
quote: All traders should keep in mind that stop-loss orders do not provide any guarantees for how and when they will be executed, and they provide no coverage when the market is closed.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Collars and Reverse-Collars', 'What Is the Trader's Risk Appetite?' (p. 85)
notes: Also relevant to the book's Chapter 2 earnings-gap example (gap 30->37) - in perps an equivalent news move would trade through the stop continuously, so the failure mode shifts to cascade/liquidation; this should inform V8 risk_rule calibration and the simulator's gap/cost model.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Overconfidence calibration (90% confidence ranges miss ~45% of the time)
mechanism: estimation_calibration: humans systematically overstate the precision of their estimates; trading systems must be built on measured distributions, not self-assessed confidence.
setup_summary: Research practice rule: whenever an edge, parameter, or probability is claimed, require a measured point-in-time distribution; treat self-assessed confidence as systematically overconfident (Eckhardt's 747-weight test: subjects targeting 90%-certain ranges missed 4-5 of 10).
trigger_invalidation: Not a trade setup.
risk_geometry: None stated.
quote: Eckhardt said that the majority of people missed about 45 percent of the questions because they were overconfident in their ability to estimate reality.
chapter_anchor: Ch.13, third Turtle class at Commodities Corporation (pp.183-184)
notes: Supports V8's honest-evidence culture: parameter/edge claims need measured distributions and frozen OOS, not analyst confidence intervals.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Light-volume test of a prior high or support level
mechanism: a retest of a level on shrinking volume shows the aggressive side's force is drained, raising double-top/double-bottom odds
setup_summary: A retest of a prior swing high on volume lower than the first test signals draining buying power (bearish, raises double-top odds - bonds example: 379k vs 504k contracts); a retest of support on light volume signals draining selling force (bullish - bonds doji-tweezers bottom, 234k vs 448k). Usually paired with small real bodies, doji, or tweezers at the level.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price returns to a windowed prior extreme on volume below the first test's volume. Invalidated if the level breaks decisively on expanding volume (rejection was wrong; the level was not defended).
risk_geometry: Entry on next-bar confirmation; stop beyond the tested level; the double-top example gives a minimum measured target (bonds: 'double top gave a minimum measured target of 90').
quote: A light volume test of a support level suggests a diminution of selling force and is, consequently, bullish. Conversely, a light volume test of a previous high is bearish since it demonstrates a draining of buying power.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 15 'Candlesticks with Volume and Open Interest', Exhibits 15.1-15.3 (pp. 241-245)
notes: The book's stated limitation - futures volume is reported a day late (p. 241) - does not apply to perps, where volume is real-time; this is one of the cleanest transfers in the book. Measured-move targeting on a confirmed double top is a falsifiable target rule.
book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

strategy_name: Value area and initiating-vs-responsive order flow (Market Profile)
mechanism: price probes advertise for the opposite side; initiating flow outside the prior value area predicts where value moves, and shrinking value areas show declining trade facilitation
setup_summary: Volume-by-time (TPO) profile defines the value area (~70% of session volume). Initiating selling - range extensions and extremes under the prior day's value area on expanding volume - should be bearish; buying below prior value is 'responsive' (expects return to value), selling below it is 'initiating' (expects value to move down). Shrinking value areas during an advance indicate the market is failing to accept higher prices as value, a top warning.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: initiating selling (extreme + range extension) under the prior value area on expanding volume. Invalidated if price is quickly rejected back into value (the initiating group is wrong; responsiveness wins).
risk_geometry: N/A - market-structure feature; profile-derived levels (value area bounds, extremes) can serve as stop/target references.
quote: Thus, if there is initiating selling activity (extremes and/or range extension), under the previous day's value area on expanding volume, it should have bearish implications.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 17 'Candlesticks with Market Profile' (pp. 259-265)
notes: Crypto perps have no designated daily open, so value-area analysis requires defining a session boundary (e.g., 00:00 UTC); the 'initial balance' concept maps to an opening-range concept. TPO-style volume-by-time is computable from trade data. The initiating-vs-responsive classification is a falsifiable auction-theory flow feature that corroborates the flow vocabulary.
book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

strategy_name: Fear-collapse quality-asset buy (capitulation)
mechanism: fear-driven selling overshoots intrinsic value on intact assets, and the correction of that misappraisal delivers the return
setup_summary: After a severe fear-driven collapse in which a fundamentally intact asset loses a large fraction of its value while the crowd extrapolates zero (GEICO -97% from $61 to $2; Wells Fargo down ~49% in a year on a regional real-estate panic), buy in size and accumulate over months-to-years. The market has misappraised the asset, not the business.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extreme price collapse combined with economics that are intact (temporary problem, not structural). Invalidation: the intact-economics premise is disproven (Fruit of the Loom-style structural decline, GEICO's near-bankruptcy from reserve mispricing), or the discount to assessed value is never achieved.
risk_geometry: Entry at market during depressed conditions, accumulated over years (GEICO bought over five years, Washington Post over 1973); no bar-level stop or target; exit = value realization; Buffett: 'a year like that... would not distress us.'
quote: Great investment opportunities come around when excellent companies are surrounded by unusual circumstances that cause the stock to be misappraised.
chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'Value Tenets' (quote p.131); Ch 3 GEICO (p.32); Ch 4 Wells Fargo (p.57-58); Ch 1 American Express (p.3)
notes: Corroborates V8's DATA_BLOCKED capitulation family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion, requires trend,volatility,history). In 24/7 perp crypto the 'temporary problem' filter is critical: deleveraging cascades produce many cheap-but-broken assets, and V8's tape cannot directly measure fundamental intactness - the main transferable observable is fear-extreme overshoot followed by reclaim.
book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

strategy_name: Share repurchase below value as accumulation signal
mechanism: when an issuer repurchases its own securities below intrinsic value, each dollar spent buys more than a dollar of intrinsic value, creating value for remaining holders and signaling rational capital allocation
setup_summary: When an issuer repurchases its own securities at a price below assessed intrinsic value, accumulate alongside: each repurchase acquires more intrinsic value per dollar spent and signals management rationality. Coca-Cola repurchased 32% of shares outstanding (since 1984) at an average $12.46 - worth ~$60B a decade later; the Washington Post repurchased 43% of its shares at an average $60.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: buyback program announced/executed below assessed intrinsic value. Invalidation: repurchase above value (destroys value per dollar), or the repurchase is financing-constrained (Fruit of the Loom-style over-leverage, 128% debt/equity).
risk_geometry: Entry at or below the repurchase price; no stop/target; hold through value realization; horizon is years.
quote: If a company's stock price is $50 and its intrinsic value is $100, then each time management buys its stock, they are acquiring $2 of intrinsic value for every $1 spent.
chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Management Tenets' - rationality / share repurchase (p.89-92); Coca-Cola buyback (p.90)
notes: Crypto analog is token buyback-and-burn / treasury repurchases below fair value as a supply-flow signal. DEFER_GATED because V8's tape lacks on-chain supply-flow data; would enter via a flow feature group (with cross_market) only if on-chain data is added to the pipeline.
book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

strategy_name: Frictional cost drag
mechanism: active turnover silently taxes returns via spreads, commissions and fees; aggregate investor returns equal business gains minus marketplace-imposed costs, so a hyperactive market is a pickpocket of the patient
setup_summary: Any strategy's live return equals gross backtest return minus per-unit costs (taker fee, funding, slippage) times turnover. Rule: before any family is promoted it must clear a cost hurdle computed as (fee + funding + slippage) x expected turnover; high-turnover families must show edge several multiples of per-unit cost. Falsifiable in V8 by charging full Binance USDM fees plus funding on every fill and re-evaluating frozen OOS.
trigger_invalidation: If an expert's OOS edge collapses to at-or-below its measured cost burden, the family is cost-drag-bound and must be gated or rejected.
risk_geometry: Not an entry geometry; cost accounting applied at fill: taker fee + funding accrual + slippage over the L1 fill-at-close model.
quote: the aggregate pre-tax rewards to our owners will equal the business gains achieved by the company less the transaction costs imposed by the marketplace—that is, commissions charged by brokers plus the net realized spreads of market-makers
chapter_anchor: Part III.A The Bane of Trading: Transaction Costs (1988), pp. 119-121
notes: Crypto perps are the worst-case environment for this: taker fees, 8h funding and slippage compound over 24/7 turnover. Directly corroborates V8's Binance USDM cost model and the 'hyperactive stock market is the pickpocket of enterprise' warning (p. 129).
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Credit-extension-by-instrument erosion (watch the lenders, not the borrowers)
mechanism: When the credit-supply side progressively degrades underwriting/leverage standards to grow loan or volume throughput, hidden fragility accumulates in the system that later converts into defaults; the top is dated by lenders losing restraint, not by any single price statistic.
setup_summary: On any market state, treat measurable easing of credit/leverage availability (in crypto perps: rising max-leverage tiers, relaxed margin/collateral rules, launch of higher-risk leveraged products, sustained positive-funding leverage build-up) with static aggregate risk metrics as a rising-fragility regime rather than a neutral condition. Burry flagged the top from the 'extension of credit by instrument' — lenders inventing new instruments to lend to people who could not otherwise afford it — while FICO/LTV aggregates stayed flat.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: observable expansion of credit/leverage availability without compensating quality. Invalidated: if the same provider subsequently tightens (raises margins, cuts leverage tiers), or if actual defaults/liquidations do not rise after the standard erosion.
risk_geometry: Not a trade; a regime filter feeding RiskGate admission and long-side still_valid logic. No entry/stop/target of its own.
quote: What you want to watch are the lenders, not the borrowers. The borrowers will always be willing to take a great deal for themselves. It's up to the lenders to show restraint, and when they lose it, watch out.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'In the Land of the Blind' (Michael Burry)
notes: The underwriting-standard mechanism transfers to perps as venue leverage policy (exchanges raised max leverage in bull phases) and funding/collateral regimes, but there is no underwriting analog and no teaser-reset; the proxy is leverage availability, OI structure, and funding. Root incentive is the originate-and-sell moral hazard: 'Any business where you can sell a product and make money without having to worry how the product performs is going to attract sleazy people.'
book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

strategy_name: Price-volume confirmation with time-normalized volume (VAT)
mechanism: a price move is more credible when volume agrees, and time-of-day-normalized volume (VAT) removes calendar skew that hides the true level of participation
setup_summary: Rising price + rising/above-average volume = bullish, trend supported; rising price + falling volume = top/consolidation warning; falling price + rising volume = bearish; falling price + falling volume = bottom warning. Volume spike at market lows = accumulation; at market highs = distribution. Compare volume to its same-time-of-day average (VAT — average of that hour/day over prior X days), not a plain moving average, because a plain MA is skewed by stale and by time-of-day structure.
trigger_invalidation: Confirmation feature only; no independent invalidation — its failure (price up, volume light) is itself a warning flag used to fade the move.
risk_geometry: Feature/confirmation input; book specifies no entry, stop, or target for volume rules alone.
quote: Price is rising and volume is rising and/or above average = bullish market; the uptrend is being supported by market participants.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'Volume at Time' and 'Intraday Volume at Time' (pp. 36-43)
notes: For perps, volume is notional and taker-split based, traded 24/7; hour-of-day and day-of-week normalization is implementable from the tape, but wash trading and venue fragmentation distort absolute volume — normalize relative to a venue-consistent baseline. Volume features belong in the participation group.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Scale trading - averaging down near historical lows without stops
mechanism: For physical commodities, production-cost and historical floors imply an eventual rebound; buying more in tranches at descending levels lowers average cost and pays off on the rebound.
setup_summary: Set a base price near historical lows; buy tranches at fixed increments below the base as price falls; use NO stops; keep buying until price bottoms and turns up, then sell the accumulated position back to the market. Requires large reserve capital; margin calls and large drawdowns can blow out undercapitalized accounts before the rebound.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis only fails permanently if the asset never rebounds; interim invalidation is margin-call/undercapitalization, not a price stop.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit buys at descending fixed increments; no stop; exit on rebound (sell accumulated tranches); open-ended holding period with roll/expiry risk in futures.
quote: You do not use stops. You keep buying on the way down until prices hit a bottom and begin to turn back up.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Scale Trading' (pp.210-212)
notes: The causal floor (production cost / physical demand) does not exist for a BTC perp, and the no-stop mandate directly conflicts with V8's RiskGate admission and stop-first risk framework. Funding accrues on a growing losing notional, and leverage converts the intended averaging-down into deleveraging-cascade exposure. Reject; the only transferable piece is tranche accumulation as a regime-gated variant of a value extreme - not worth a family.
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Buy when macro-fear is at a peak (contrarian accumulation, ignore forecasts)
mechanism: Fear peaks create price discounts that the fundamentalist exploits; macro forecasts are an expensive distraction, and the best purchases are made exactly when apprehensions are maximal.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, after a sharp drawdown accompanied by a realized-volatility spike and elevated participation (the observable fear proxy), enter LONG while apprehensions are at a peak rather than deferring; ignore all macro/political forecasts. Falsifiable: define fear proxy = drawdown depth percentile AND realized-vol percentile over a window; enter only when both are extreme.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = fear proxy at extreme (deep drawdown + vol percentile); invalidation = price fails to reclaim the prior swing low or fear persists beyond expiry without stabilization, indicating capitulation exhaustion did not occur.
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; stop below the fear-swing extreme (structure); target R-multiple; long expiry given slow sentiment repair.
quote: we have usually made our best purchases when apprehensions about some macro event were at a peak. Fear is the foe of the faddist, but the friend of the fundamentalist.
chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.207-208
notes: Directly extends the existing backlog family capitulation_exhaustion (src/v8/experts/capitulation.py, DATA_BLOCKED pending derivatives tape). Crypto is sentiment-driven 24/7 with funding and long-liquidation cascades that make fear peaks mechanically observable (negative funding, long liquidation sweeps), so the proxy is more concrete than in equities. No statistical case is made in the book (anecdotal), hence NARRATIVE.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Investor gains equal business gains in the end (closed-system conservation)
mechanism: Aggregate investor gains must equal the underlying business gains over time; price/value divergence only redistributes between buyers and sellers, and 'generally, the sophisticated have an edge over the innocents'.
setup_summary: A falsification frame for V8: in perpetuals the closed system is even stricter than equities — there is no earnings accrual, and funding makes the market explicitly zero-sum minus fees. Therefore any claimed edge is a redistribution from the less-sophisticated side, and the baseline expectation is that the average participant loses to costs. Falsifiable: an expert family's net OOS return must exceed the cost drag (fees+funding+slippage) of simply holding exposure, or the 'edge' is illusory.
trigger_invalidation: Applies to V8 verdicts, not to entries: no economic claim can be registered unless net-of-cost OOS return beats the passive-exposure baseline; this is a precondition for any registry promotion.
risk_geometry: N/A - evaluation frame; use the simulator's Binance USDM cost model to compute the passive baseline.
quote: in the end, investor gains must equal business gains.
chapter_anchor: Part V.E Intrinsic Value, Book Value, and Market Price, pp.189-190
notes: Also: 'When the stock temporarily overperforms or underperforms the business, a limited number of shareholders receive outsized benefits at the expense of those they trade with.' This is the strongest structural caution in the book for any V8 claim and supports the existing NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM default and frozen-OOS verification discipline.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Panic-liquidity provision (be greedy when others are fearful)
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, long after a panic signature: forced-deleveraging flush (deeply negative funding, open-interest contraction via liquidations, capitulation-sized down bars) - the moment when 'naked swimmers call Berkshire'. Entry next-bar close; thesis is that loss-aversion sellers have overpaid to exit and the flush is exhausted; exit on structure reclaim or expiry.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: panic state (extreme negative funding + liquidation cascade + climax down-bar). Invalidation: price keeps making new lows with expanding participation/volume - the flush is regime change, not exhaustion.
risk_geometry: Book states no explicit entry/stop/target; only the discipline of fast decisive action in panics ('the time for that transaction was NOW'). For V8: entry next-bar close, stop beyond panic low or ATR multiple, expiry in bars, capped heat.
quote: Berkshire is the 800 number when there is a panic in the markets
chapter_anchor: 2013 annual meeting, '1-800-BRK-Deal'; 2011 'Fear and Opportunity'
notes: Corroborates the existing backlog family 'capitulation' (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion) and adds the premium-harvest framing: the counterparty to loss-aversion exits gets paid. Crypto perps lack a fundamental 'value' anchor, so 'cheap' must be proxied by flow/liquidation data, not intrinsic value.
book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017
